newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court rules to ease public sector pay claim.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court rules to ease public sector pay claim.

text.p: Brazil's supreme court struck down a key article of a presidential decree seeking to restrict public sector workers from claiming a 28.9 percent pay rise issued to a small group of civil servants earlier this year, a court official said.

The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) ruled 6-5 against the clause of the decree which requires individuals seeking pay rises through court actions to place a deposit before beginning proceedings, the STF spokesman said.
"The court believes the article blocked free access to the justice system," the spokesman said.
Earlier this year, the STF awarded a 28.9 percent pay rise to 11 civil servants who claimed they were entitled to an increase of that amount awarded to the armed forces in 1993.
That decision has spawned a flurry of similar cases involving tens of thousands of federal government employees and pensioners who claim they are also entitled to the increase.
Officials from the government's economic team have said increases for all the one million employees and pensioners of the federal government could upset Brazil's attempt to reduce public spending.
The STF maintained two other articles of the decree. The action was brought by the government-allied Liberal Party.
